executiveSummary: GM0523 passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service numerical contract. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 19,123 residents, 25 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, two BRT settlement labels, three in-boundary rail stations, 32 transit stop areas and two A15 logical border links are coherent; neighbourhood population differs from the independently rounded municipality total by only 13. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The river preset reports 3.067454 m-like inundation stress, 11,253 affected residents and exact service values at T+24, remaining critical with the same direct flood and 12,067 affected at T+72, without a selected dike-ring-16 breach/overtopping case, Merwede boundary condition, connected LIWO footprint, arrival, duration, recession or dewatering path. The standalone coastal source correctly produces zero direct water, but cannot be interpreted as an all-clear for the Benedenrivieren transition, wind setup, backwater or drainage combinations. Eight unrelated hazard families reuse the same neighbourhood order: Wielwijk-noord ranks first for storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire despite the municipality and water board documenting a forecast-driven pluvial protocol, historic local wateroverlast, peil-area lowering and extra pumps. Thirty-six public water-register objects include RWZI Hardinxveld-Giessendam, Kolffgemaal, sewer and surface-water pumps, sluices and weirs, yet none supplies connected or live water-chain state to the exact service outputs. The graph omits the Hardinxveld-Werkendam/Sleeuwijk/Gorinchem ferry and rail operations; current public information also reports a MerwedeLingelijn speed restriction and reduced stopping pattern through 21 April 2027. External acute care, Stedin/Oasen, telecom, education/shelter, hazardous-goods and first-72-hour resource dependencies remain uncalibrated. Official layers, registers, schedules and plans must retain publisher, edition/valid time, coverage, licence and NoData semantics; no record must never become zero, safe, dry, open or operational.

evidenceSources.title: Wijken en buurten 2025, bestuurlijke gebieden, BAG woonplaatsen and BRT TOP10NL
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundaries and statistics; generated municipality inputs retrieved 2026-08-31
supports: Nationwide machine-readable CBS OData and PDOK OGC sources support GM0523 identity, Hardinxveld-Giessendam, Zuid-Holland, 19,123 residents, density 1,134/km², 18.8 percent aged 65+, 2,235 one-person households, 25 neighbourhoods and one active BAG place.

A current full-boundary query returns feature e72b7c0c-935c-5fde-b3b4-d254871a29e9, a MultiPolygon with 872 coordinate positions. The deployed overview has 53 positions and is suitable for national selection/aggregation, not hydraulic or asset-containment decisions.

Published neighbourhood rows sum to 19,110 residents, thirteen below the municipality total (-0.068 percent), consistent with independently rounded values. Core counts are complete, while district heating and public charging cover 0/25 and remain null/Unknown.
CBS and BRT reuse is CC BY 4.0; BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Editions must be joined by official code and valid date rather than labels or proximity.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 — overstroming dijktrajecten 16-1 t/m 16-5
evidenceSources.edition: Definitief concept 16 May 2024 for the 2025–2028 planning period
supports: Hardinxveld-Giessendam is explicitly one of the municipalities protected by dike sections 16-1 through 16-5, formerly dike ring 16; the protected Alblasserwaard/Vijfheerenlanden area is approximately 39,230 ha with approximately 240,000 residents.

The regional profile treats flooding, extreme weather, critical-service interruption, dangerous substances and transport disruption as distinct mechanisms. It is static planning evidence, not a selected breach, current warning, probability, live resource inventory or T+72 outcome.

The safety-region scope crosses municipal and provincial borders, so evacuation, reception, medical care, repair and supply cannot be inferred from the GM0523 boundary or its road degree. No standard reuse licence or live event API is stated for the planning PDF.

evidenceSources.title: Calamiteitenplan wateroverlast and Watertakenplan Hardinxveld-Giessendam 2024–2033
supports: The municipal calamity plan coordinates municipality, water board and safety region from weather forecasts and explicitly allows preventive placement of additional pumps before extreme rainfall.

The 2024–2033 Watertakenplan describes wastewater, rainwater, groundwater and surface water as distinct duties, 14.6 km of watercourses and 75 culverts, vulnerable sewer areas and a design target of 29.4 mm/hour for new sewer systems; a T=100+10 percent 66 mm/hour shower may occupy public space but should not damage buildings or block through roads for long where floor levels meet the stated assumption.

These targets and plans are infrastructure/planning evidence. They do not prove event-time pump availability, soil/storage state, sewer capacity at a cell, safe roads, action completion or recovery. The reviewed pages state no machine interface, fixed update cadence or standard reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Rivierenland and Het Waterschapshuis via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Hardinxveld extreme-rain measures, Nieuwe Waarden Alblasserwaard and IMWA/DAMO water registers
evidenceSources.edition: Operational notice 19–22 June 2026; NWA project status accessed 3 September 2026; register snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: On 19 June 2026 the water board placed extra pumps and temporarily lowered Hardinxveld-area water levels because 30–40 mm/hour and locally more than 50 mm were forecast. The pumps were removed unused on 22 June. This proves a forecast-triggered action protocol and uncertainty, not a permanent asset or simulated incident.

The Nieuwe Waarden Alblasserwaard project says current Nederwaard/Overwaard water is supplied and discharged via Kinderdijk, while a new Hardinxveld boezem canal/pump is being developed as a second Merwede route. The design project was still in procedure/construction preparation in 2026 and must not be treated as completed capacity.

The deployed HWH IMWA/DAMO cache assigns 36 records to GM0523: five sewer pumps, one wastewater-treatment site, ten surface-water pumps, four sluices and sixteen weirs, including RWZI Hardinxveld-Giessendam, Kolffgemaal, Peulensluis and Damsluis. Status, missing capacity and duplicate/related records must remain explicit.

Machine-readable OGC services https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are CC BY-SA 4.0. Contributor completeness/cadence vary; registers establish location/type/status, not connectivity, direction, compatible capacity units, live controls, quality, power/backup or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Landelijk Informatiesysteem Water en Overstromingen (LIWO)
supports: LIWO exposes professional flood-scenario layers and candidate breach context. IPLO explicitly states that correct interpretation needs specialist water-management knowledge.

A simulation-ready selection must preserve release, scenario/model dates, source water, defence and breach/overtopping state, variant, native CRS/resolution, units, NoData, depth, velocity, arrival, duration and clock mapping. A candidate breach marker or maximum-depth layer is not a live breach, forecast or evacuation order.

Availability is release-driven rather than an incident feed; reuse/licence conditions must be resolved per downloaded layer before redistribution. Missing or transparent cells remain NoData, never dry.

evidenceSources.title: NWB/rail infrastructure and current Hardinxveld ferry and MerwedeLingelijn operations
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; GTFS snapshot 30 August 2026; Qbuzz restriction valid 17 July 2026–21 April 2027; Riveer current page accessed 3 September 2026
supports: The deployed graph contains two feature-traceable A15 logical links, to Gorinchem and Sliedrecht, plus Hardinxveld Blauwe Zoom, Hardinxveld-Giessendam and Boven Hardinxveld rail stations and 32 scheduled-transit stop areas. NWB/ProRail CC0 geometry establishes identity, not incident-time capacity or opening.

Riveer officially serves the Gorinchem–Sleeuwijk–Hardinxveld–Werkendam route and warns that weather, calamities and maintenance can alter sailings. This cross-Merwede foot/bicycle lifeline is absent from the graph; the timetable/app has no reviewed stable licensed emergency-status API.

Qbuzz currently reports a rail speed restriction from track subsidence, no bicycles/fatbikes through 21 April 2027, and only half-hour stopping at Hardinxveld-Giessendam during the quarter-hour pattern. The Papendrechtsebrug closure also diverts traffic to A15/A16. These dated modes/constraints do not enter the solver.
Scheduled geometry is neither vehicle/vessel availability nor evacuation, emergency, freight, ambulance or repair capacity. An absent NDW/GTFS match is Unknown, not open or unavailable.

evidenceSources.title: Public capacity-planning, telecom, education and acute-care context

The deployment assigns 31 RDI antenna installations, fourteen marked mobile communication, and eleven DUO education locations. Records do not establish coverage, backhaul, power/backup, occupancy, shelter designation/capacity, supplies or opening.

residualLimitations: VRZHZ and municipal plans establish mechanisms, roles and doctrine, not a current incident, probability, forecast, completed action, loss calibration or live resource inventory.

No reviewed source selects a dike-16 breach/overtopping location, Merwede hydrograph/datum, defence state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession or dewatering path for this exercise.
LIWO layers are official scenario-library products requiring expert interpretation, not observations or forecasts; per-layer licence/reuse and NoData must be resolved.
HWH/DAMO objects and capacities have contributor/field gaps and cannot establish connected potable, wastewater or surface-water topology, controls, quality, power/backup or restoration.
The 19–22 June 2026 pump deployment is historical operational evidence of a protocol, not a persistent asset, current action or calibration event; pumps were removed unused.
NWA is a developing system change. A project page, design decision or enabling utility work is not commissioning evidence and cannot add simulated capacity.
